title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class rho with lazily evaluated steps (prefix-product trie, 3,527-instruction key kernel, Winograd-paired, one full multiplication per six steps)

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT in the van Oorschot-Wiener trail form with exponents recovered by replay, as in the parent package gt-dprestart-replay, but with the multiply-only R=24 adding walk evaluated lazily: each walk keeps an explicit base y and a node of a precomputed prefix-product trie of depth 6 over the 288 twisted multipliers, its current element is y*Pi_node, the class key of that element is computed from the w^1 coefficient c_1(y*Pi_node)=sum_k y_k gamma_k(Pi_node) formed by Winograd's pairing with a per-base stored xi_y=sum_i y_2i y_2i+1 and a per-node stored xi_gamma (3 Fp2 products), by the 3,527-instruction straight-line kernel lazy.s (3,425 for root.s at the root, which also stores xi_y), and the base is made explicit by one 12,774-instruction multiplication mul.s every sixth step; multiplier index (from the whole low word, bits 0..63), distinguished-point bits (64..143) and 112-bit fingerprint (144..255) are read from the key minimum K; 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes square the smaller-key class; a pre-debit 192-bit work meter, report log, matcher, sampler and caps as in the parent; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds, in the ideal model, with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^123.947 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000) on every run, including setup (the table and the 2^49.02-leaf trie, two units per node), pairings, walk starts and fresh starts, distinguished-point handling, escapes, detection delay, matching (sort, duplicate removal, replays and pair checks), output and verification. A complete block of six steps is charged 34,872 instructions (root step 3,595, lazy step 3,697, lazy step with the flush 16,489; 170 of every-step work each), c=0.2906 units per step, and a partial block less per step; fruitless-cycle waste is charged as eps=0.032933 (1.25 times the H2 model: 2-cycles at 1/288 per step, all other cycles up to length 64 at 6.17e-5, longer useless walks below 2^-108.71 per step at DP density 2^-80). The ledger is 2^123.94681 and 2^123.947 is the least thousandth above it; a run has at most 2^125.73 iterations because every block of iterations, with the escape or report that ends it, is charged at least c per iteration. Peak memory is below 2^62 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^50.04 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the random-mapping heuristic for rho walks with the conservative correction 1/(1-1/R) (model success 0.4002 at S=2^125.68269), at least 0.39689 after the loss terms of proof.md section 4, every one a computed bound and none an allowance: the report cap (2^55) carries a Markov share of 0.00162 at 617 times its expected count, the restart cap (2^29) 0.00102 at 986 times, the pair budget (2^8) 2^-11 at 2,048 times, the restart cap's own worst case is charged as 1.841e-4 of the iteration maximum in steps spent on restarts, the waste in fruitless closed walks is bounded by Freedman's martingale inequality under deferred decisions (tail below 2^-1000), and detection, single-trail collisions, ties and the sampler add their computed bounds; expectations use only linearity, the lemma that a fresh class's labels are uniform given everything revealed (H2) and, for the at most 0.546 expected merges, H1's pair-collision rate, so no step assumes independence of iterations, reports, restarts or trails; H2 models the 256 bits of K the rule reads (bits 0..255) as a random function of the class and the indices and twists as independent uniform; it is supported by the emulated kernels, the production lazy walk run step by step against an eager walk in the real BLS12-381 GT with distinguished points, records, fresh starts and replay of every record, statistics of the bits of K on production classes, and by toy-field censuses of the complete algorithm. No production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: BLS12-381 GT identities (Frobenius, the 12-key formula against explicit conjugates, canonical representative, orders, Granger-Scott). Part K: generate the four straight-line kernels in memory and run them in the shipped emulator on real GT elements against a big-integer reference (counts 12,774 / 6,777 / 3,527 / 3,425 on every call). Part C: the production lazy walk (R=24, trie depth 6) in the real GT with every key from emulated root.s/lazy.s and every flush and escape from emulated mul.s/sqr.s, with distinguished points at a test density, records, fresh starts, compared at every step with an eager walk, and every record replayed from its start pair to the same fingerprint with its canonical pair verified. Part G: statistics of the bits of K read by the rule on production classes. Part B: the complete algorithm (trails, report log, heapsort matcher, replay, escapes, meter) in toy fields, with the success metric in meter units (every iteration before the collision at one step of c, escapes at their largest meter prices). Part E: pair-collision law. Part F: exact fruitless-cycle bounds at R=24. Part D: the ledger, caps, budget inequality and claim on integers. Part S: the bounded sampler; flags_check.py: multiword compares under AArch64 NZCV. No production costs are measured by running the attack.
